 South Dakota's minimum wage to increase by 45 cents in 2027
 SDPB | 
 By
 SDPB News Staff 
 Published November 18, 2026 at 10:36 AM CST
 SDPB 
 South Dakota’s minimum wage is set to increase to $12.30 per hour on Jan. 1.
 That’s an increase of 45 cents from its current rate of $11.85, according to the Department of Labor. The hourly minimum wage for tipped employees will be $6.15. Workers' wages plus tips must equal at least the state's full minimum wage.
 In 2014, South Dakota voters passed an initiated measure increasing the state’s minimum wage. The measure included annual increases based on the U.S. Department of Labor’s consumer price index.
 When that law took effect the following year, it increased the minimum wage from the federal minimum of $7.25 to $8.50. Since then, the minimum wage has increased by an average of a little over 3% per year, though the exact amount changes year per year based on the federal data. The 3.7% increase coming in 2027 is slightly higher than the historical average.
